description.short_caption: Fundoscopic image showing optic disc swelling and blurred margins.
description.detailed_description: This is a fundoscopic image of the retina, showing the optic disc with notable swelling and blurred margins. The surrounding retinal vessels appear prominent, and there is a hazy area around the optic disc, suggestive of possible papilledema or optic neuritis. The image is centered on the optic nerve head, with a reddish-orange background typical of the retinal fundus.
visible_findings: hazy area around the optic disc

Case_08025/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Fundoscopic exam, 10 weeks after admission, with macular star.

description.short_caption: Fundoscopic image showing macular star pattern.
description.detailed_description: This fundoscopic image shows the retina with prominent vascular structures and the optic disc visible on the right. A macular star pattern is evident, characterized by radial streaks of exudates extending outward from the macula. The image is well-focused, with clear visualization of retinal vessels and the surrounding structures. The macular star is indicative of retinal involvement, often associated with conditions such as hypertensive retinopathy or infectious processes.

description.short_caption: Fundoscopic image showing retinal vasculature and optic disc.
description.detailed_description: This is a fundoscopic image of the retina, showing the optic disc on the right side of the image with a bright yellow appearance. The retinal vasculature is clearly visible, branching out from the optic disc. The macula is located centrally, appearing slightly darker than the surrounding retina. The image appears to be free of significant hemorrhages, exudates, or other obvious pathological findings.
visible_findings: optic disc with bright yellow coloration
retinal vasculature branching from the optic disc
